yogas.name: Ikkavala
yogas.rule: All seven planets occupy kendras (1,4,7,10) or panapharas (2,5,8,11); apoklimas (3,6,9,12) are empty.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.1

yogas.name: Induvara
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.2

yogas.name: Ithasala
yogas.rule: Two planets in Tajika aspect within orb with the faster planet less advanced in its sign (applying). Poorna: gap <= 1°; Vartamana: within orb; Bhavishyat: the faster planet enters the orb after moving 1° or less.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.3

yogas.name: Ishrafa
yogas.rule: Two planets in Tajika aspect within orb with the faster planet more advanced in its sign (separating).
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.4

yogas.name: Nakta
yogas.rule: Two planets without Ithasala/Ishrafa between them each have a present Ithasala with a third planet faster than both.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.5

yogas.name: Yamaya
yogas.rule: Two planets without Ithasala/Ishrafa between them each have a present Ithasala with a third planet slower than both.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.6

yogas.name: Manahoo
yogas.rule: A present Ithasala in which Mars or Saturn (not one of the pair) is conjunct the faster planet within the faster planet's deeptamsha.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.7

yogas.name: Kamboola
yogas.rule: A present Ithasala between two planets (neither the Moon), and the Moon has a present Ithasala with one or both of them.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.8

yogas.name: Gairi-Kamboola
yogas.rule: A present Ithasala (neither planet the Moon); the Moon, in the last degree of its sign and without Ithasala with either, forms Ithasala with one of them once it enters the next sign.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.9

yogas.name: Khallasara
yogas.rule: The lagna lord occupies the sign between the Moon and another planet X and has no present Ithasala with the Moon or with X.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.10

yogas.name: Radda
yogas.rule: A present Ithasala in which either planet is debilitated, retrograde or combust.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.11

yogas.name: Duphali-kuttha
yogas.rule: A present Ithasala in which the slower planet is strong (exalted, own sign or Pancha-vargiya Bala >= 10) and the faster planet is weak (not exalted, not own sign, Pancha-vargiya Bala < 5).
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.12

yogas.name: Dutthottha-davira
yogas.rule: Both planets of a present Ithasala are weak (debilitated, in an inimical sign, or Pancha-vargiya Bala < 5) and one of them has a present Ithasala with a strong third planet (exalted, own sign or Pancha-vargiya Bala >= 10).
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.13

yogas.name: Tambira
yogas.rule: A planet in the last degree of its sign, without present Ithasala with a slower planet, forms Ithasala with that slower planet once it enters the next sign.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.14

yogas.name: Kuttha
yogas.rule: A planet in the lagna is aspected by another planet that is in its own or exaltation sign and placed in a kendra or panaphara.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.15

yogas.name: Durupha
yogas.rule: A present Ithasala in which both planets are afflicted: in a dusthana (6, 8, 12), combust, retrograde or debilitated.
yogas.source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section); P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.16

source: Tajika Neelakanthi, Samjna Tantra (shodasha-yoga section), rules as given in P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, "Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach" (2000), ch. 29 §29.2.1-29.2.16; aspects and deeptamshas ch. 28 §28.2; Pancha-vargiya Bala thresholds ch. 28 §28.4.6. conventionNotes: Seven grahas only (Sun..Saturn); the nodes and outer planets take no part. Houses are whole signs from the chart ascendant.
Faster/slower follows the natural speed order of the source (ch. 29 fn. 83), not the instantaneous speed.
Aspects are sign-based Tajika aspects (1, 3/11, 4/10, 5/9, 7). The 2/12 semi-sextile (a neutral aspect in ch. 28 §28.2, used in some ch. 29 examples) is counted only with includeSemiSextile.
Orb rule MUTUAL: each planet within the other's deeptamsha, i.e. gap <= min of the two (§29.2.3 worked example). Alternative: HALF_SUM (engine TajikaYogasCalculator).

Retrogression (§29.2.3 special notes): a retrograde faster planet that is behind is separating, and one that is ahead is applying. The "about to turn retrograde" refinement and the "smaller gap under retrogression" remark are not quantified by the source and are not applied.
Nakta, Yamaya, Manahoo, Kamboola, Radda and the later yogas build on present (Vartamana/Poorna) Ithasala only, not Bhavishyat.
"Last degree of a sign" (Gairi-Kamboola, Tambira) = 29° or more, direct motion; the future Ithasala is tested with the planet at 0° of the next sign.
Manahoo uses conjunction only, as the source advises; aspect-based Manahoo is option manahooByAspect.
Duphali-kuttha: the source's wording (faster strong / slower weak) and its worked example (slower strong / faster weak) disagree; the worked example is implemented.
Strong = exalted, own sign or Pancha-vargiya Bala >= 10 ("strong", §28.4.6); weak = Pancha-vargiya Bala < 5 ("weak", §28.4.6), plus debilitation / inimical sign where the yoga text names them.

Durupha: the source requires both Ithasala planets to be in a dusthana or combust or retrograde or debilitated; its example (both debilitated, not in dusthanas) shows any one affliction per planet suffices.
Khallasara: "the sign between" is read as Moon and X two signs apart with the lagna lord in the sign between them (either direction). Other authors define Khallasara differently.
Kuttha: the aspect is the sign-based Tajika aspect; the evidence row shows the orb but it is not required.
Combustion uses the engine's calculateCombustion orbs (planets/combustion.ts).
Verse numbers of Tajika Neelakanthi are not cited (the edition used for verse numbering is not fixed); section numbers of the cited English text are given instead.
